# Full-space affine buffers with negative-power normalization

This is a fixed-epsilon UNPENALIZED joint bad-attainment theorem for a new parameter class. The parameter is positive affine in BOTH integer-base and continuous coordinates. Its negative-power normalization prevents a limiting zero even at a sampled fiber boundary. The proof establishes positive-parameter attainment; it does not import the old projective-energy alignment, proper-own-cut conclusions, or any Gamma payment.

## 1. Setting and normalization

Fix d>=1, N=d+1, and an exponent r>=d. Let P be a finite complete canonical lattice base. Affine functions below are functions on aff(P) times R^d, identified by their restrictions to this affine space; coefficients in irrelevant perpendicular directions are not parameters.

For a positive compatible family K_z, let

    C=conv union_(z in P) ({z} times K_z),
    mu(A)=sum_(z in P) vol_d(A_z),
    M=sum_z |K_z|.

For an affine L(z,X) strictly positive on the COMPACT canonical body C, impose

    <L^(−r)>:=M^(−1) integral_S L^(−r)dmu=1.                (1)

Use the aligned-power expression

    f_L(z,X)=[L(z,X) E_(K_z)(X)/M]^(1/N),                 (2)

and the same actual within-fiber covariance norm G_K(u) in the buffered cap displacement epsilon f_L G_K(u). Pure-base caps are unchanged. Although (2) uses the same exponent as the old energy buffer, its gradient alignment changes, as recorded in Section 6.

The real-base energy root F=E^(1/d) is jointly concave by the existing ordinary energy theorem. Since positive affine L is concave, weighted geometric-mean concavity gives joint concavity of

    f_L=M^(−1/N) F^(d/N) L^(1/N).

Positivity on all of C is retained, not merely positivity at fiber centroids. The construction and (1) are invariant under the actual common continuous affine coordinate changes and affine continuous shears used in the compactness reduction: transport L as a scalar affine function. The common determinant in mu and M cancels.

## 2. A uniform interior ball at the mixed centroid

Let a compact family of positive fiber bodies satisfy M=1, V_z>=v>0, K_z contained in R Ball, with the base P fixed. Its canonical hulls have relative dimension dim aff(P)+d. Put

    m_K=integral_S (z,X)dmu=sum_z V_z(z,g_z).

Then m_K lies in the relative interior of C, and there is one radius rho>0 such that every C in the family contains the relative ball of radius rho about m_K.

For interiority, suppose a nonzero supporting affine function h>=0 on C vanishes at m_K. Since its nonnegative mixed integral is h(m_K)=0, it vanishes almost everywhere on every positive full-dimensional fiber. Its continuous coefficient is therefore zero and its base affine restriction vanishes at every z in P. It is consequently zero on the full relative affine span, contradiction.

For uniformity, the finite fiber centroids and volumes are continuous under the positive Hausdorff limits, and canonical hulls converge in Hausdorff distance. The support-distance formula

    min_(||v||=1)[h_C(v)−v.m_K]

is therefore continuous on the compact family. It is positive by the preceding interiority and hence has a uniform positive minimum. This uses the relative unit sphere; no ambient rank assumption is hidden.

Consequently, if an affine h is nonnegative on C and has arithmetic mixed mean <h>=1, then h(m_K)=1 and its linear coefficient has norm at most 1/rho. Its constant coefficient is bounded too because m_K is bounded. Thus arithmetic-normalized positive affine parameters are uniformly bounded in coefficient space.

## 3. The exact inverse-power boundary divergence

Let D be any positive d-dimensional convex body and h a nonnegative affine function on D with h(x_0)=0 at some x_0 in D. Then

    integral_D h^(−r)dx=infinity       whenever r>=d.      (3)

If h vanishes identically on D, this is immediate. Otherwise write its nonzero continuous coefficient as c. Choose an interior ball in D and a positive level s_0 of h through that ball. Its intersection with the level plane contains a positive (d−1)-dimensional ball B_0. The cone conv(x_0,B_0) lies in D. Its section at h=s has (d−1)-area (s/s_0)^(d−1)|B_0| for 0<s<s_0. Coarea therefore bounds the integral below by

    [|B_0|/(||c|| s_0^(d−1))]
                      integral_0^s_0 s^(d−1−r)ds=infinity.

For d=1 the base ball is a point with H_0 measure one, giving the same interval proof. At r=d the divergence is logarithmic.

The assertion survives JOINT variation. Suppose D_j converges in Hausdorff distance to positive D, h_j is affine and positive on D_j, and its coefficients converge to h. Convex-body indicators converge almost everywhere; every interior point of D eventually belongs to D_j. The nonnegative functions equal to h_j^(−r) inside D_j and zero outside therefore satisfy Fatou's inequality. If h has a zero on D, (3) yields

    liminf_j integral_(D_j) h_j^(−r)dx=infinity.           (4)

There is no requirement that the same zero point belong to D_j. When h vanishes only on a limiting boundary face, the divergent limiting integral comes from positive h values arbitrarily near that face, so a null boundary does not invalidate Fatou's argument.

The exponent condition is sharp for this mechanism. On the standard d-simplex, let t=sum_i X_i and take h_s=t+s. If 0<r<d, then as s decreases to zero,

    <h_s^(−r)> -> d/(d−r)<infinity,

because the uniform t density is d t^(d−1) on [0,1]. Thus normalized positive affine functions may approach a vertex-zero function with finite scale. This is a boundary-divergence limitation, not a bad-depth counterexample.

## 4. Every escape has large values at enough actual centroids

Let K_j belong to the compact family of Section 2, and let L_j satisfy (1). Set

    A_j=<L_j>,       h_j=L_j/A_j.

By Section 2, after a subsequence h_j converges in coefficient space to an affine h, nonnegative on the limiting C, with <h>=1. The normalization gives EXACTLY

    A_j=<h_j^(−r)>^(1/r),       L_j=A_j h_j.              (5)

If h is strictly positive on C, its minimum stays uniformly positive on the nearby C_j. Bounded-kernel integration and fiber-volume convergence imply that the scale in (5) converges to a finite positive number. Hence L_j has a finite strictly positive limit on C.

Otherwise h vanishes somewhere in C. Because C is the convex hull of the sampled fibers and h is affine, it vanishes on at least one of those actual fibers. Section 3 then gives A_j→infinity.

There are two cases.

(a) The continuous coefficient of h is nonzero. Its restriction to every positive fiber is nonconstant and nonnegative. Its average there, h(z,g_z), is STRICTLY positive. Since actual centroids converge,

    L_j(z,g_jz)→infinity for EVERY z in P.                 (6)

(b) The continuous coefficient is zero. Then h depends only on the base and its zero set is a nonempty proper face F of conv(P). At every sampled p outside F,

    L_j(p,g_jp)→infinity.                                 (7)

These cases account for every failure of positive finite parameter compactness. In case (a), a touching continuous boundary does not leave a set of uninflated centroid fibers; all centroid values diverge. In case (b), the occupied-parity complement-face arithmetic theorem supplies the required outside center.

## 5. Fixed-epsilon UNPENALIZED joint bad attainment

Retain exactly the original minimal-bad-base compactness assumptions from `candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb` and `candidate 108870e8f9aac2e9`. In particular choose b<Gamma_d/k(P) above an original bad reference value. Every original sublevel family beta_0<=b has a normalized representative in one compact positive class A, with M=1, uniform V_z>=v, bounded fibers, and proper-closed-minor quotas

    V(T)<=b k(T)/Gamma_d<k(T)/k(P)                         (8)

also at limits. These are established dependencies, not a new unconditional bad-body existence claim.

Fix epsilon>0 and take pairs with beta_epsilon(K_j,L_j)<=b. Since buffering is nonnegative, beta_0<=beta_epsilon, so their bodies compactify in A. Suppose the full-space parameters escaped. Section 4 gives divergence at all centroids in case (a). The ordinary occupied-parity weighted BASE-center theorem provides a fixed base p of limiting depth at least 1/k(P). In case (b), the independently audited complement-face quota theorem, applied with (8), provides such a p outside F. In either case L_j(p,g_jp)→infinity.

At that actual centroid, E_jp(g_jp)=V_jp>=v. The covariance minimum sigma_j=min_(||u||=1)G_j(u) stays uniformly positive. Therefore, for this FIXED epsilon,

    epsilon [L_j(p,g_jp)V_jp]^(1/N) sigma_j>=2R            (9)

eventually. All fibers with nonnegative base drift from p are wholly captured by every such buffered cap. Equivalently one may apply the actual whole-own-fiber capture lemma. Including pure-base caps, the buffered depth at this source equals its actual base depth.

Base depths are continuous in the finite weights, because they are minima over finitely many base traces. Thus

    liminf beta_epsilon(K_j,L_j)>=1/k(P)>b,

contradiction. The full affine parameters consequently have a positive finite subsequence limit on C.

At such a limit, uniform positivity on the actual compact C_j, coefficient convergence, energy continuity and covariance continuity give the same all-direction uniform slab comparison as in the affine-base attainment source. Thus beta_epsilon is continuous. The bad sublevel of full-space pairs is compact modulo the permitted actual body normalizations.

Whenever a reference pair has value below b, the infimum over ALL positive compatible families and ALL full-space affine L>0 satisfying (1) is attained. For all sufficiently small epsilon, L=1 supplies such a reference. Writing beta_0^* for the original fixed-base infimum,

    beta_0^*<=inf_(K,L) beta_epsilon(K,L)
                     <=beta_0^*+epsilon L_slab R,         (10)

by testing the original minimizer with L=1. Hence minimum VALUES converge to the original minimum.

No uniform-in-epsilon bound on L, no proper-own-section conclusion, and no Gamma response payment is inferred.

## 6. Changed source gradient and exact fixed-body normalization derivative

Write c for the continuous coefficient of L. The energy identity is grad_x E=N E a_E. Direct differentiation of (2) gives

    grad_x log f_L = a_E + c/[N L(z,X)].                  (11)

Thus the old exact alignment with the ENERGY optimizer a_E is LOST whenever c is nonzero. A critical-buffer normal balance involves the vector in (11), not a_E alone. In particular no old projective-centroid, boundary-potential, or cap-cover statement may silently substitute a_E into that balance.

The new chart nevertheless remains globally positive on the actual source fiber. At an interior mark y, concavity of F=E^(1/d) gives

    T_E(x)=1+(N/d) a_E.(x-y)>=0 on K_z.

Consequently the new source tangent denominator is exactly

    1+[a_E+c/(N L(y))].(x-y)
        =(d/N) T_E(x)+(1/N) L(x)/L(y)>0 on K_z.

This establishes a legitimate projective chart, not centroidality of its image. The latter is the missing premise for importing the old projective boundary payment.

At a fixed body, let phi be any affine full-space function. Normalize L+t phi by its negative-power mean. Since <L^(−r)>=1, the exact tangent is

    dot L=phi−L A_phi,
    A_phi=<L^(−r−1)phi>,
    dot f_L/f_L=(1/N)[phi/L−A_phi].                       (12)

Indeed the normalizing scale is <(L+t phi)^(−r)>^(1/r), whose derivative at zero is −A_phi. Positivity of L on compact C makes both signs of every affine perturbation legal for sufficiently small t. These identities do not require cap regularity.

For clarity, under the SEPARATE established finite regular-singleton continuation hypotheses, normalize the old group weights rho_ij by sum_j rho_ij=1 and its continuous normals by G_K(u_ij)=1. Let S_ij>0 be the actual threshold coareas of its regular caps, and put B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij. A group at the marked point Y_i with delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i has the corresponding raw upper-cover derivative

    q_i'=(delta_i/N)[phi(Y_i)/L(Y_i)−A_phi].               (13)

If such groups cover all current maximizing marks and the parameter is a local minimum, finite separation gives eta_i>=0, sum eta_i=1, such that, for every affine phi,

 sum_i eta_i delta_i phi(Y_i)/L(Y_i)
      =(sum_i eta_i delta_i)<L^(−r−1)phi>.                (14)

Testing constants and coordinates shows that the tilted FULL mixed mean

    integral_S (z,X)L^(−r−1)dmu / integral_S L^(−r−1)dmu   (15)

belongs to the convex hull of the selected marked sources. This is only a conditional continuation consequence; it is not imported for supporting/atomic groups without their proper response theorem. The tilted measure in (15) is not the original uniform mixed measure, and no uniform target-marginal lift is asserted.

The later companion `candidate 137cd11c6631be8a` proves a stronger necessary mean inclusion at an unpenalized joint local minimum below 1/k(P), using an exact parameter decrease followed by atomic hinge cleanup. That proof avoids regular group derivatives altogether. It does not alter the conditional scope of the derivative identity (13).

## 7. Scope

The negative-power mean upgrades parameter compactness because it detects every actual fiber-boundary zero for r>=d. This differs from both geometric-mean base normalization and an argument depending only on sampled centroid values.

The resulting attained setting permits genuine continuous affine parameter variations, but it changes the source-gradient balance. Recovering a physical Gamma payment with that changed balance is a separate obligation. Equations (11)–(15) state the new interface precisely without claiming that the earlier aligned-energy machinery remains applicable unchanged.
